message.content:
## Observations

1. Each insertion preserves the relative order of all elements already in the array.
2. If the insertions are undone from \(N\) down to \(1\), then just before undoing insertion \(i\), the remaining elements occupy \(i\) slots in the final array, and \(i\) is in the \(P_i\)-th of those slots from the left.
3. Marking each unassigned slot with \(1\) and each assigned slot with \(0\) makes the \(k\)-th unassigned slot the first position whose prefix sum reaches \(k\). A Fenwick tree can find that position by binary lifting and update its mark, each in \(O(\log N)\) time.
4. The bounds \(1 \le P_i \le i\) guarantee a valid choice even when only one slot remains or when the first or last unassigned slot is requested.

## Solution sketch

> Each insertion preserves the relative order of all elements already in the array.

1. Read \(N\) and the insertion positions. Allocate an answer array of length \(N\) and initialize a Fenwick tree with a \(1\) at every position. Work backward so that assigning a later number to its final slot leaves the earlier numbers in their original relative order among the unassigned slots.

> If the insertions are undone from \(N\) down to \(1\), then just before undoing insertion \(i\), the remaining elements occupy \(i\) slots in the final array, and \(i\) is in the \(P_i\)-th of those slots from the left.

2. Process \(i\) from \(N\) down to \(1\). Write \(i\) into the \(P_i\)-th unassigned slot, then mark that slot as assigned. The unassigned slots now represent the array just before insertion \(i\), so the same rule applies to the next number.

> Marking each unassigned slot with \(1\) and each assigned slot with \(0\) makes the \(k\)-th unassigned slot the first position whose prefix sum reaches \(k\). A Fenwick tree can find that position by binary lifting and update its mark, each in \(O(\log N)\) time.

3. To perform each selection, use Fenwick-tree binary lifting to find the largest prefix with sum strictly less than \(P_i\); the next position is the desired slot. After writing \(i\), subtract \(1\) at that position in the tree. The \(N\) selections and updates take \(O(N\log N)\) total time, and the tree, input positions, and answer use \(O(N)\) space.

> The bounds \(1 \le P_i \le i\) guarantee a valid choice even when only one slot remains or when the first or last unassigned slot is requested.

4. Use the same selection rule for every valid rank, with no special case for \(N=1\) or for either endpoint. Once all slots are assigned, print the answer from left to right, separated by spaces.
